title: Moderna RSV Shot 82% Effective Against Hospitalization in Veterans 50 and Older, but Infection Protection Fell With Age - Medical Daily

analysis.time: The study was published on Nov 14, 2026, and the vaccination period was tracked from Oct. 31, 2026, with up to 24 weeks of follow-up. The findings were reported as RSV season builds across the country.
analysis.location_and_population: The study involved U.S. veterans 50 and older who received care through the Veterans Health Administration. The analysis included 74,926 vaccinated veterans and 286,425 unvaccinated veterans.
analysis.event: Moderna's mRNA vaccine against respiratory syncytial virus (mResvia) was found to be 81.8% effective at preventing RSV-related hospitalization among U.S. veterans 50 and older, according to a large Veterans Affairs study in JAMA Network Open reported by CIDRAP. Protection against any documented infection was lower, at 60.3%, and protection against infection also dropped steeply with age.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The vaccine was 82.9% effective in veterans ages 50 to 59 but only 28.6% effective in those 80 and older. The study is among the first large real-world looks at how the mRNA vaccine performs outside clinical trials. The FDA approved mResvia in May 2024 for adults 60 and older and expanded approval in June 2025 to adults 18 to 59 at increased risk of RSV lung disease.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The findings are based on a target trial design, which tries to mimic a randomized trial using health records. The study was reported by CIDRAP, and the results are part of ongoing analysis. A separate VA analysis posted as a preprint estimated 87% effectiveness against RSV hospitalization using a different design, but this has not been peer reviewed. Whether mResvia's protection holds into a second or third season is unknown.
